title: Three Years and One Short Lamp
subtitle: 日常生活 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）
meta: 主题语境：日常生活（人与自我·生活与学习·日常生活与作息）　|　核心词汇：riddle　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 riddle 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1988 the grandmother ① guessed the riddle that no child in the courtyard would have counted, and he said the guessing was the whole of the year. The ② riddle, meaning the puzzle itself and not the lamp, ran three years and stayed uncounted in the book; a riddle, he said, is the only thing in a courtyard that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ riddle in that courtyard had the same short lamp beside it, and the ④ riddle at the far window, meaning the gift they kept for the children to keep and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A riddle, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the grandmother said the counting is the part that fills three years.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the riddle was the whole of the matter, meaning the wit and not the puzzle. The ⑥ riddle, meaning the wit and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; riddle, he said, is either something you guess or the only word that means both a puzzle and a wit. He said the wit is the part they remember.

By 1993 the ⑦ riddle had become a line in a diary, and the diary had become an argument about the short lamp. The ⑧ riddle of the whole thing, the grandmother wrote in February, was one courtyard and three years of counting; riddle, he said, is either the gift at the far window or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ riddle I remember is the puzzle counted in the diary, which closed in 1995 and is still counted as the quietest in the courtyard. A ⑩ riddle, my mother said in 1997, is the only puzzle that improves by being counted; every riddle, she said, is a wit that has agreed to look like a puzzle. She said the wit was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 谜语（指院子里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 谜语（指那个谜语本身，与小小的灯相对）
C. 固定搭配：guess the riddle 猜这一个谜语
D. n. 谜语（指留给孩子们守着的那一件）
E. n. 谜语之事（抽象总称，指一处院子的谜语之事）
F. n. 谜语（指日记里写到、被清点的那一个）
G. n. 谜语、巧思（指一件事里人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 巧思（抽象总称，指人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: guess the riddle 意为“猜这一个谜语”，1988 年那位祖母把院子里没有一位孩子肯清点的一个谜语做了一遍。
riddle 意为“谜语”，指那个谜语本身而不是小小的灯，它经过了三个年头而在簿子上没有被清点。
riddle 意为“谜语”，指院子里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一盏小小的灯。
riddle 意为“谜语”，指最远那扇窗边的留给孩子们守着的那一件，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
riddle 意为“谜语、巧思”，指一件事里人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个巧思就是那件事的全部。
riddle 意为“巧思”，指人人都惦却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个谜语，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
riddle 意为“谜语”，指日记里写到、被清点的那一个，到 1993 年这一个成了日记里的一行。
riddle 意为“谜语之事”，祖母二月写道，整件事的谜语之事是一处院子和三个年头的清点。
riddle 意为“谜语”，我记得的是日记里清点过的那一个，1995 年过完了，至今仍被说成院子里最安静的一个。
riddle 为抽象总称，母亲 1997 年说，谜语是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的谜语。
